name: Populism
summary: Populism, in the leading scholarly definition, is a thin-centred ideology that divides society into the pure people and a corrupt elite and says politics should express the people's general will. It has little program of its own and attaches to host ideologies, usually socialism on the left and nationalism on the right. It favors direct popular decision-making and distrusts institutions that check the majority.
scope: The ideational core as defined by Cas Mudde and Cristobal Rovira Kaltwasser, plus the historical US People's Party (Omaha Platform, 1892) as a primary example. Economic, immigration and cultural answers are mostly left neutral because they come from host ideologies; right-wing and left-wing variants are noted where they differ. Excludes the economic-mismanagement and purely rhetorical-style uses of the term.

public-ownership.rationale: The Omaha Platform called for public railroads, telegraph and telephone, yet market-friendly populists exist; adherents split by host ideology.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Omaha Platform demanded a graduated income tax and left populists attack the very wealthy, but right populists often do not share this.

unions-good.rationale: The Omaha Platform sought an eight-hour day and defended workers against capital; modern right populists vary.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Anti-establishment populism targets monopolies and big business (the Omaha Platform opposed corporate land and railroad power), though economic views depend on the host ideology.

strong-leader.rationale: Right-wing populism is associated with executive power concentration and bypassing institutions, but leaders are not essential to the ideational core and left strands differ.

state-harmful.rationale: Populists want the state returned to the people, not abolished; the Omaha Platform asked for more government action, such as public railroads.

empower-police-military.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

reviewHistory.rationale: Right-wing populism often favors law and order and authority.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Right populism stresses protecting national identity and traditional values; left populists use inclusive notions of nationality.

gradual-change.rationale: Populists are hostile to established institutions and the political establishment, so inherited institutions are not treated as a reason for slowness.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration restriction is central for right-wing populism, which Mudde treats as the nativism it is combined with; left populism does not hold it, and the Omaha Platform also urged restricting immigration.

free-trade.rationale: Populists commonly express skepticism of globalization and cosmopolitan economic agendas.

nation-first.rationale: Right populists oppose cosmopolitan and globalizing agendas and favor the native nation, while left strands are more varied.

open-borders.rationale: Populist movements generally do not favor open borders, though left strands do not stress restriction.

experts-over-public.rationale: Populism pits the common people against elites and holds that the people know what is best, so deferring to experts over the public is rejected.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic nationalism and protectionism are common in right-wing populism, while left populists are skeptical of globalization.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Omaha Platform called land the heritage of the people and sought to reserve it for settlers over speculators, a small-owner ideal for the historical movement.

democracy-best.rationale: Populists present themselves as the true democrats and defend majority rule, though they are skeptical of liberal checks that limit what the majority can do.

direct-votes.rationale: Populists favor referendums and popular initiatives as ways for the people to decide directly, and the 1892 Omaha Platform endorsed the initiative and referendum.

natural-rulers.rationale: The moral core of populism is that ordinary people are pure and that elites are corrupt, so a natural class of rulers is rejected.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Populism puts the people's voice and will at the center, so leaving the country is not treated as the main check on government.

media-academia-power.rationale: Populists portray the media as part of the establishment disconnected from the public.

single-common-good.rationale: Populism rests on a general will and a homogeneous people, and is described as moralistic and resistant to compromise rather than as balancing group interests.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The corrupt elite set against the pure people is the defining claim of populism, and the Omaha Platform preamble says corruption dominates the ballot-box, legislatures and Congress.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Populism is a thin-centred ideology with no stated position here; left populists favor accountability for the powerful while right populists back law and order.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Populism is a thin ideology with no stance of its own on this; right-wing variants lean toward it and left-wing ones against, so adherents are split.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Populism takes this from its host ideology; left variants lean yes and nationalist ones no, so neutral.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Populism takes this from its host ideology; nativist variants favor limits, liberal ones do not, so neutral.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Populism says politics should express the people's general will and champions popular sovereignty, so authority rests on the people's consent.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Populism is thin-centred and has no epistemology; anti-elite rhetoric sometimes disputes expert claims but adherents are split.

trade-surplus.rationale: Host ideologies decide trade views, so adherents are split; right populists lean protectionist and left populists vary.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: No stated position; populist appeals against elite domination echo the idea but the doctrine does not define freedom this way.

separated-powers.rationale: Populism distrusts institutions that check the majority will, and favors direct popular decision-making over divided power.

vanguard-party.rationale: Populism holds that the people already share a general will and needs no revolutionary vanguard, though charismatic leaders play a large role.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Left populists stress the poor and right populists stress the native people; the thin ideology itself does not decide, so adherents are split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Left to the host ideology; left and right populists differ on housing policy.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Left to the host ideology; left populists back strikes while some right populists favor limits.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Host-dependent: right-wing populism is often nativist, left-wing populism is not.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Populism favors popular decision-making but its sources do not treat sortition as a core demand.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Populism distrusts checks on the majority, yet it also distrusts concentrated state power; host ideologies decide.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Left to the host ideology; the Omaha Platform favored state intervention but this was not specific to prices.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Host-dependent: right populism favors long waits while left populism does not.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Populism takes its cultural answers from its host ideology, so adherents are split on censoring art.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: As a thin-centred ideology populism takes its answer from its host; right-wing populists are often sceptical of alliances and left-wing ones vary.

people-in-arms.rationale: No stated position; host ideologies split on guns and armies.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: No stated position; it depends on the host ideology, as right-wing nativism and left-wing universalism differ.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Right-wing populists lean towards descent-based citizenship, but populism itself is silent and left variants differ.

minority-language-support.rationale: Nativist right populism opposes it while left populism may support it, so adherents split.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Populism is thin-centred and takes its answer from its host ideology: left variants favour cancellation, right variants oppose it.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Left populists favour aid and right populists want it cut, so adherents are split.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Thin-centred ideology with no stated position; it takes its answer from its host ideology, so adherents are split.

collective-defense.rationale: Thin-centred ideology with no stated position; adherents split by host ideology and many are sceptical of alliances.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: No stated position; populists distrust party elites, but strong party-aligned leaders are common, so adherents are split.

region-keeps-system.rationale: No stated position; adherents are split by host ideology between centralism and local self-rule.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Sovereignty belongs to the people and their general will, not to a ruler, so a sacred ruler of divine descent contradicts the core idea.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Split: the Omaha Platform and left-wing populists want a graduated income tax, while some right-wing populists favour flat taxes.

character-from-environment.rationale: Thin-centred ideology with no stated position; adherents are split by host ideology.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Populism favors direct popular decision-making and distrusts institutions that check the majority, so a balance of few and many is disfavored.

leader-cult.rationale: Populists often favor strong charismatic leaders, but this is a style, not a defining claim; adherents are split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Thin-centred ideology with no stated position; adherents are split.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Territorial claims come from nationalist hosts; left populists do not share them, so adherents split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The ideational definition makes the general will of the people supreme, and scholars note populists are hostile to institutions that check the majority.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Right-wing populism favors economic nationalism, while left populists often do not, so adherents split.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Populism takes its answer from its host ideology: nativist right-wing forms centre the nation, left forms do not.

patriotic-education.rationale: Populism is thin-centred; right-wing populism backs patriotic schooling while left forms are split.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Populism takes its answer from its host ideology, and left and right variants differ.

public-money-creation.rationale: Only the Omaha Platform (s3) demands a government-issued currency without banks; the thin ideology has no monetary doctrine, and right-wing populists take theirs from host ideologies.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Populism has no theory of capitalist crisis; its hosts differ.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Populism takes its answer from its host ideology; right-wing forms often favour it, left forms do not.

delink-world-market.rationale: Populism takes its answer from its host ideology; right-wing forms favour economic nationalism and left forms vary.

minority-veto.rationale: Mudde and Rovira Kaltwasser describe populism as majoritarian and hostile to institutions that constrain the popular will.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Populism calls for active mobilisation of the people to take politics back from elites.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Populists accuse elites of manipulating the people, but the thin ideology has no theory of how rule is maintained.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Left populism may agree and right populism may not; set by the host ideology.

native-born-offices.rationale: Nativism is separate from the populist core; right populists agree and left populists mostly do not.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Right populists favor economic nationalism, left populists are split; set by the host ideology.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Populist majoritarianism cuts one way and left hosts the other, so adherents are split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Right populists often stress national sovereignty and sceptical of universal models, others do not; adherents are split.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Thin-centred ideology with no stated position; right and left hosts differ.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Thin-centred ideology with no stated position; hosts split between state pensions and market reform.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Omaha Platform calls land the heritage of the people and wants excess corporate holdings reclaimed for actual settlers, though it stops short of abolishing private ownership.

single-official-language.rationale: Right-wing nativist populism may favor it and left-wing populism does not; adherents are split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Thin-centred ideology with no stated position; hosts differ.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Omaha Platform opens by charging that corruption dominates the ballot box and legislatures in favor of corporate power, which is a core grievance against the elite.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Right populists restrict foreign funding while left populists do not; the thin core takes no position.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The thin core is silent; populists distrust elite law-makers but many call for popular rule of law.

non-intervention.rationale: Right populists favor non-intervention while left populists vary; the thin core does not decide it.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Populism targets a corrupt elite, not a minority, though right-wing variants add nativism; the core does not endorse minority conspiracy claims.

religious-nation.rationale: Right populists often link nation and faith, while left populists do not; the core has no position.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Populism favors direct popular decision-making, and the Omaha Platform demanded the initiative and referendum.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Populism is thin-centred and takes its credit policy from its host ideology; the Omaha Platform wanted state money and postal savings rather than mutual banks.

property-franchise.rationale: Populism says politics should express the general will of the whole people, so a wealth qualification on voting contradicts it.

reification.rationale: Left populists share the critique of markets while right populists reject it, so adherents are split.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Populism has no stated position on religious doctrine; it takes its answer from its host ideology, so adherents are split.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Omaha Platform attacked concentrated corporate and monied power as a threat to the people's liberty, but modern populism is mostly neutral on economics because it depends on the host ideology.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Populism is a thin-centred ideology that takes no position on sexuality; right and left variants differ, so it is neutral.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Populism is majoritarian and holds that politics should express the people's general will, so guaranteed shares for minority communities cut against it.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Populism does not address charity versus state aid; left populists favor public programs and right populists favor community and national solidarity, so adherents are split.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Populism has no position on extinction risk and adherents are split, with some distrusting expert agendas that put it ahead of the people's present concerns.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Populism takes no position on religious office; it is host-ideology dependent and adherents are split.

rent-control.rationale: Left populism supports rent caps and right populism is split; as a thin ideology it takes its answer from the host.

recognise-genocide.rationale: No stated position; right and left variants differ on historical memory.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Right populism invokes the nation's heartland and tradition while left populism does not; split by host ideology.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Some right-populist movements honour martyrs but the thin ideology itself has no position.

god-not-male.rationale: No stated position; left and right hosts differ.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Right populism favours national preference, left populism does not; the thin ideology is split.

independent-unions.rationale: Populism is a thin-centred ideology; its host ideologies differ on unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Left populists might agree, but the thin ideology takes no position on what counts as socialism.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Thin-centred; no stated position, and anti-elite attitudes cut both ways here.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Thin-centred; anti-elite currents may favor it but others back state control.

person-over-state.rationale: Populism puts the people's general will first but has no stated position on individuals versus the state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Thin-centred; right populists often invoke religion and left populists do not.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Right populists often define the people ethnically and left populists do not, so adherents are split.

racial-pride.rationale: Right populists often endorse national or ethnic pride and left populists do not, so adherents are split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Thin-centred; populists of both hosts split on foreign interventions.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Populism is thin-centred and takes its view of the nation from its host ideology, so language as the basis of a nation is left split.

free-public-college.rationale: Left-wing populists back free higher education while right-wing populists are split, and the thin ideology has no position of its own.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Populism has no stated position on pollution taxes, and populists often oppose such taxes as burdens on ordinary people while some left-wing forms back them.

future-generations.rationale: Populism is a thin-centred ideology with no stated view on duties to future generations, so the answer comes from the host ideology and adherents are split.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Populism has no stated position on whether women bring distinct values, and host ideologies divide on it, so adherents are split.

arms-reduction.rationale: Populism has no stated position on arms; right-wing forms favor strong defense and left-wing forms are more mixed, so adherents are split.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Populism has no stated position on soldiers refusing orders; the host ideology decides, and nationalist hosts oppose refusal while leftist hosts may support it.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Populism takes economic positions from its host ideology: left populism backs unions, right populism is often indifferent or hostile.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Populism has no stated position on tax credits; the host ideology decides, so adherents are split.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Left populists favor reforming the world economy for poorer countries while right populists favor national interest and reject global rules, so adherents are split.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Populism wants the elite replaced and the people's will expressed, but has no stated line on smashing versus using the state; hosts differ.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Populism has no economic blueprint of its own, and the question is left to host ideologies.

sacred-nation.rationale: Populism has no stated position here; right-wing populist hosts treat the nation as sacred while left-wing hosts do not.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Left populism supports relief for debtors while right populism is split, so adherents are divided.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Populism has no stated position here; leftist hosts may accept the core-periphery analogy, while others reject it.

public-service-media.rationale: Populism sets the people against elites, and its views on public media vary: some adherents want publicly funded media, others see it as an elite institution.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: No stated position; left populists favor regulation while right populists distrust courts and agencies alike.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: No stated position; adherents are split by host ideology.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Right populists often favor tough sentencing, but left populists and others do not, so adherents are split.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Populism prizes the people's general will over procedure and distrusts institutions that check the majority, so it resists a purely procedural definition.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Populism is thin-centred and takes its religious view from its host ideology, so adherents are split.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Populism has no program of its own on planned economies; left populists may defend them and right populists would not, so adherents are split.

indirect-election.rationale: Populism favours direct expression of the people's will and distrusts intermediaries, and the Omaha Platform pushed for more direct election of officials.

national-church-status.rationale: A national church is a host-ideology matter, with right populists often backing it and left populists opposing it, so adherents are split.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Populism has no stated position here; right populists tend to favour restricting migration and left populists differ, so adherents are split.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Right-wing populists such as Duterte endorse it and left populists reject it; the thin ideology itself is silent, so adherents are split.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Populism distrusts intermediary institutions and favors direct expression of the general will, though left populists stress initiative and referendum more than a leader.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The Omaha Platform preamble attacks corruption and privileged railroad and monopoly interests, and populism opposes the corrupt elite.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Populism is a thin-centred ideology that takes its view of just distribution from its host ideology, so adherents are split.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The Omaha Platform backed a graduated income tax, but a financial transactions tax is not a populist position as such and depends on the host ideology.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Racism's role depends on the host ideology; right-wing populists often downplay it and left-wing ones do not.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Populism has no stated view; its stress on the people's will over legal limits points both ways, so adherents are split.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Left populists may back automation with shared gains and right populists defend existing jobs; the answer comes from the host ideology.

material-over-identity.rationale: Left populists put economic issues first while right populists stress cultural identity; adherents are split by host ideology.

police-more-powers.rationale: Right-wing populism often favors law and order and authority. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Populism takes its answer from its host ideology; right-wing forms often favour it, left forms do not. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Political elites are corrupt and out of touch with ordinary people.
missingStatements.rationale: The belief that a corrupt elite stands against the pure people is the defining claim of populism, and the Omaha Platform preamble says corruption dominates the ballot-box, legislatures and Congress.

notes: Left and right strands answer economic and cultural items in opposite ways, so those are scored neutral. The profile is expected to have few stated positions.
